claim: Six others are shared; these two are DRC's alone.
because: The count of six held only from the 2009 vintage, when Corton (from Prince Florent de Merode's vines) was added, up to the 2018 vintage. It stopped being true when Corton-Charlemagne, from vines leased from Bonneau du Martray, joined the range with the 2019 vintage. DRC now releases seven shared grands crus besides its two monopoles: Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant, Grands-Échézeaux, Échézeaux, Corton, Corton-Charlemagne and Montrachet. It also owns about 0.17 ha of Bâtard-Montrachet, which it does not sell.
fix: Its other grands crus (Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant, Grands-Échézeaux, Échézeaux, Corton, Corton-Charlemagne from 2019, Montrachet, and a tiny unreleased Bâtard-Montrachet) are shared; these two are DRC's alone.
